items.informal_name: Algebra Equivalence for Multivariate Polynomials over Fin(n+1) and Option(Fin(n))
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {σ : Type u_1} [inst : CommSemiring R] {n : ℕ} (e : σ ≃ Fin n) (φ : MvPolynomial (Option σ) R),
  (MvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv R n) ((MvPolynomial.rename ⇑(e.optionCongr.trans (finSuccEquiv n).symm)) φ) =
    Polynomial.map (MvPolynomial.rename ⇑e).toRingHom ((MvPolynomial.optionEquivLeft R σ) φ)
items.informal_description: The algebra equivalence between multivariate polynomial rings over $\text{Fin}(n+1)$ and polynomials in one variable with coefficients in multivariate polynomials over $\text{Fin}(n)$ commutes with renaming variables via the bijection $\text{Fin}(n+1) \simeq \text{Option}(\text{Fin}(n))$. Specifically, applying the $\text{finSuccEquiv}$ equivalence after renaming variables through this bijection is equivalent to applying the polynomial map induced by the $\text{optionEquivLeft}$ equivalence, preserving the algebraic structure over a commutative semiring $R$.

items.informal_name: Existence of Finite Renaming for Multivariate Polynomials
items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} {R : Type u_4} [inst : CommSemiring R] (p : MvPolynomial σ R),
  ∃ n f, ∃ (_ : Function.Injective f), ∃ q, p = (MvPolynomial.rename f) q
items.informal_description: For any multivariate polynomial $ p $ over a commutative semiring $ R $ with variables indexed by a type $ \sigma $, there exists a natural number $ n $, an injective function $ f : \{1, 2, \dots, n\} \to \sigma $, and a polynomial $ q $ in $ n $ variables such that $ p $ equals the polynomial obtained by renaming the variables of $ q $ according to $ f $. This expresses that every multivariate polynomial depends on only finitely many variables.

items.informal_name: Algebra equivalence between multivariate polynomials over Fin(n+1) and polynomials in one variable with coefficients in multivariate polynomials over Fin(n)
items.type:
(R : Type u) →
  [inst : CommSemiring R] → (n : ℕ) → MvPolynomial (Fin (n + 1)) R ≃ₐ[R] Polynomial (MvPolynomial (Fin n) R)
items.informal_description: The algebra equivalence between the ring of multivariate polynomials with variables indexed by $\text{Fin}(n+1)$ and coefficients in a commutative semiring $R$, and the polynomial ring in one variable whose coefficients are multivariate polynomials over $R$ with variables indexed by $\text{Fin}(n)$. This equivalence is constructed by renaming variables via the bijection $\text{Fin}(n+1) \simeq \text{Option}(\text{Fin}(n))$, mapping the $\text{none}$ case to the outer polynomial indeterminate and $\text{some } k$ cases to inner variables, with the inverse given by substituting renamed variables. The operation preserves addition, multiplication, and scalar multiplication by elements of $R$.

items.informal_name: Existence of Finite Subset Representation via Renaming
items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} {R : Type u_4} [inst : CommSemiring R] (p : MvPolynomial σ R),
  ∃ s q, p = (MvPolynomial.rename Subtype.val) q
items.informal_description: For any multivariate polynomial $ p $ over a commutative semiring $ R $ with variables indexed by $ \sigma $, there exists a finite subset $ s \subseteq \sigma $ and a polynomial $ q $ in the multivariate polynomial ring over $ R $ with variables indexed by $ s $, such that $ p $ is equal to the renaming of $ q $ via the canonical inclusion map from $ s $ to $ \sigma $.

items.informal_name: Existence of Common Finite Subset for Renaming Two Multivariate Polynomials
items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} {R : Type u_4} [inst : CommSemiring R] (p₁ p₂ : MvPolynomial σ R),
  ∃ s q₁ q₂, p₁ = (MvPolynomial.rename Subtype.val) q₁ ∧ p₂ = (MvPolynomial.rename Subtype.val) q₂
items.informal_description: For any two multivariate polynomials $ p_1, p_2 \in R[\sigma] $, there exists a finite subset $ s \subseteq \sigma $ and polynomials $ q_1, q_2 \in R[s] $ such that $ p_1 $ and $ p_2 $ are obtained by renaming $ q_1 $ and $ q_2 $ via the canonical inclusion $ s \hookrightarrow \sigma $. This means every pair of multivariate polynomials can be simultaneously expressed as renamings of polynomials over a shared finite set of variables.

items.informal_name: Equality of Supported Subalgebra and Range of Renaming Inclusion
items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} {R : Type u} [inst : CommSemiring R] (s : Set σ),
  MvPolynomial.supported R s = (MvPolynomial.rename Subtype.val).range
items.informal_description: For a commutative semiring $ R $ and a type $ \sigma $, given a subset $ S \subseteq \sigma $, the subalgebra of the multivariate polynomial ring $ R[\sigma] $ consisting of polynomials supported on $ S $ is equal to the image of the renaming map induced by the inclusion $ S \hookrightarrow \sigma $. This establishes that polynomials with variables restricted to $ S $ coincide with those obtained by renaming variables through the canonical inclusion of $ S $ into $ \sigma $.

items.type:
{σ : Type u_1} →
  {τ : Type u_2} → (R : Type u_4) → [inst : CommSemiring R] → σ ≃ τ → MvPolynomial σ R ≃ₐ[R] MvPolynomial τ R
items.informal_description: Given a bijection $ f : \sigma \simeq \tau $ between variable types, this defines an $ R $-algebra equivalence between the multivariate polynomial rings $ R[\sigma] $ and $ R[\tau] $. The equivalence is constructed by renaming variables according to $ f $, with the inverse equivalence given by renaming via $ f^{-1} $. This operation preserves polynomial addition, multiplication, and scalar multiplication by elements of $ R $, ensuring compatibility with the algebra structure. The bijection of variables induces a bijection of polynomials that respects all algebraic operations.

items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} {τ : Type u_2} (R : Type u_4) [inst : CommSemiring R] (f : σ ≃ τ) (a : MvPolynomial σ R),
  (MvPolynomial.renameEquiv R f) a = (MvPolynomial.rename ⇑f) a
items.informal_description: Given a bijection $ f : \sigma \simeq \tau $ between variable types, there exists an $ R $-algebra equivalence between the multivariate polynomial rings $ R[\sigma] $ and $ R[\tau] $. This equivalence is constructed by renaming variables according to $ f $, with the inverse equivalence given by renaming via $ f^{-1} $. The operation preserves polynomial addition, multiplication, and scalar multiplication by elements of $ R $, ensuring compatibility with the algebra structure.

items.name: MvPolynomial.rename
items.type:
{σ : Type u_1} →
  {τ : Type u_2} → {R : Type u_4} → [inst : CommSemiring R] → (σ → τ) → MvPolynomial σ R →ₐ[R] MvPolynomial τ R

items.name: MvPolynomial.renameEquiv
items.type:
{σ : Type u_1} →
  {τ : Type u_2} → (R : Type u_4) → [inst : CommSemiring R] → σ ≃ τ → MvPolynomial σ R ≃ₐ[R] MvPolynomial τ R

items.name: MvPolynomial.coeff_rename_mapDomain
items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} {τ : Type u_2} {R : Type u_4} [inst : CommSemiring R] (f : σ → τ),
  Function.Injective f →
    ∀ (φ : MvPolynomial σ R) (d : σ →₀ ℕ),
      MvPolynomial.coeff (Finsupp.mapDomain f d) ((MvPolynomial.rename f) φ) = MvPolynomial.coeff d φ

items.name: MvPolynomial.coeff_rename_embDomain
items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} {τ : Type u_2} {R : Type u_4} [inst : CommSemiring R] (f : σ ↪ τ) (φ : MvPolynomial σ R) (d : σ →₀ ℕ),
  MvPolynomial.coeff (Finsupp.embDomain f d) ((MvPolynomial.rename ⇑f) φ) = MvPolynomial.coeff d φ

items.name: MvPolynomial.rename_monomial
items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} {τ : Type u_2} {R : Type u_4} [inst : CommSemiring R] (f : σ → τ) (d : σ →₀ ℕ) (r : R),
  (MvPolynomial.rename f) ((MvPolynomial.monomial d) r) = (MvPolynomial.monomial (Finsupp.mapDomain f d)) r

items.name: MvPolynomial.coeff_rename_ne_zero
items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} {τ : Type u_2} {R : Type u_4} [inst : CommSemiring R] (f : σ → τ) (φ : MvPolynomial σ R) (d : τ →₀ ℕ),
  MvPolynomial.coeff d ((MvPolynomial.rename f) φ) ≠ 0 → ∃ u, Finsupp.mapDomain f u = d ∧ MvPolynomial.coeff u φ ≠ 0

items.name: MvPolynomial.coeff_rename_eq_zero
items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} {τ : Type u_2} {R : Type u_4} [inst : CommSemiring R] (f : σ → τ) (φ : MvPolynomial σ R) (d : τ →₀ ℕ),
  (∀ (u : σ →₀ ℕ), Finsupp.mapDomain f u = d → MvPolynomial.coeff u φ = 0) →
    MvPolynomial.coeff d ((MvPolynomial.rename f) φ) = 0

items.name: MvPolynomial.degreeOf_coeff_finSuccEquiv
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} [inst : CommSemiring R] {n : ℕ} (p : MvPolynomial (Fin (n + 1)) R) (j : Fin n) (i : ℕ),
  MvPolynomial.degreeOf j (((MvPolynomial.finSuccEquiv R n) p).coeff i) ≤ MvPolynomial.degreeOf j.succ p
